ownerThemes.theme: An owner of ten months calls it a great basic garment machine bought for about $400 and would recommend it.
A forum thread on upgrading within Janome praises the HD5000 at about $499, noting the extra presser foot notch for thick fabric and that it is mechanical with 18 stitches.
HD series buyers ask which of the HD1000, HD3000 and HD5000 is worth it; replies frame the HD5000 as the same core machine with more stitches, wider zigzag and a quilting kit.

editorial.verdict: The HD5000 is the top mechanical HD: the HD3000 body with a 7 mm zigzag, one-hand needle threader and seven feet including a quilting kit.
editorial.whoFor: A beginner or garment sewist who wants Janome's aluminum body and is willing to pay about $100 over the HD3000 for the wider stitch and the quilting accessories.
editorial.skipIf: You want speed (860 spm is the ceiling), a computerized stitch panel, or you sew straight seams only and would not use the extra width.

checks.title: 18 or 19 stitches
checks.body: Janome's page says 18 including the one-step buttonhole; some dealers count 19. It is a counting difference, not a different machine.

checks.title: White, Black Edition or school trade-in
checks.body: Ken's lists new, Black Edition, classroom and school trade-in units under similar titles. Confirm condition and bundle before comparing prices.

checks.title: Is the HD3000 enough
checks.body: The two share body, speed and feed. The HD5000 adds 0.5 mm of zigzag, a needle threader and quilting feet. Straight-seam sewists can save the difference.

realCost: Walking foot if the quilting kit in your bundle does not include one
Denim and leather needles size 16 to 18

faqs.q: How many stitches does the HD5000 have?
faqs.a: Janome's page lists 18 including a one-step buttonhole. Some dealer spec blocks count 19.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the HD5000 and HD3000?
faqs.a: Same body and 860 spm. The HD5000 has a 7 mm maximum stitch width versus 6.5 mm, a one-hand needle threader and seven feet including a quilting kit. Comparison sites put the gap at about $100.

faqs.q: Is the HD5000 good for quilting?
faqs.a: It has a drop feed lever for free motion and ships with a quilting attachment kit and guide bar. Throat space is not published, so it is a small-project quilter.
Dealer copy claims multiple denim layers and an extra-high presser foot lift. Janome does not publish a layer count, so treat it as a claim.
860 stitches per minute per dealer spec copy.

faqs.q: How much does the HD5000 weigh?
faqs.a: 18.7 lb per Ken's Sewing Center spec block; dimensions W 16 x H 11 x D 7 in.

faqs.q: Does the HD5000 have a needle threader?
faqs.a: Yes, Janome lists a built-in one-hand needle threader.
No dealer price appeared in the results captured. Owners cite about $499. Confirm at an authorized Janome dealer.
Janome America states 25 years materials and workmanship, 5 years electrical, 1 year labor.
